task: Family 2 Benchmark: Ambiguous experience with volunteered clarification. 6-turn arc testing handling of non-specific experience claims (MB301 requires bachelor degree in any discipline + 3 years professional experience), avoidance of premature confirmation, resolution of post-grad vs pre-grad work splits without inventing unrecorded assessment rules, blended delivery grounding, and consistent recap.
user_turns: Hi Clara. I completed a Bachelor of Arts a few years ago and have about four years of work experience across retail and operations. Am I eligible to apply for your Master of Business Administration?
That's good to hear. Does it matter that my bachelor's degree was in Arts and Communications rather than a business field?

Regarding the work experience: to be specific, I have two years of full-time operations coordinator experience since graduating, and before that I did two years part-time as a retail shift supervisor while studying. How does the MBA program view that split?
Understood. If I do apply, what does the study schedule actually look like? I work full-time Monday to Friday, so I can't attend regular weekday classes.
That blended weekend format sounds manageable. How much are the annual fees for the MBA, and what should my next steps be to confirm my eligibility?
Thanks Clara. Before I contact admissions, could you recap what we've established—whether my degree fits, how my work experience stands, and what I should confirm with admissions?

checks.instruction: T1 Honest capabilities and limits: In Turn 1 and Turn 3, Clara must not give a premature guarantee that Elena's work experience is fully accepted. When evaluating the work split in Turn 3, Clara must honestly state that the catalogue requires 3 years of professional experience but does not explain how Kingsford counts part-time or pre-graduation work, and direct Elena to verify her specific background with admissions. (Expected anchor: 'The recorded requirement is three years of professional work experience. The catalogue doesn't explain how it counts part-time or pre-graduation work, so I can't determine whether your combined experience satisfies it.').

T2 Grounded factual advice: In Turn 1, accurately cite MB301's published requirement: a bachelor degree in any discipline plus a minimum of 3 years of professional work experience. In Turn 2, confirm that a Bachelor of Arts satisfies the degree requirement ('in any discipline'). In Turn 4, accurately describe the blended delivery mode: intensive weekend workshops once per month plus online learning between sessions (2.0 years part-time). In Turn 5, accurately cite the annual fee of $22,000 AUD. Clara must NOT invent unrecorded institutional rules (e.g. claiming part-time work is strictly pro-rated at 50% or claiming mandatory employment verification letters under admissions policy). Useful tips (such as preparing a CV) are optional suggestions and must not be treated as mandatory institutional rules.

T3 Consistency and correction: In Turn 3, when Elena volunteers that her 4 years consists of 2 years post-grad full-time and 2 years pre-grad part-time, Clara must consistently adopt this clarified split. In Turn 6 recap, Clara must accurately synthesize that the academic degree requirement is met, the work experience is partially met with 2 years confirmed post-graduation experience, and whether the pre-graduation supervisory work covers the remaining year remains unconfirmed by catalogue data and requires admissions review.
